newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians disagree on Norilsk tender terms.
newsitem.headline: Russians disagree on Norilsk tender terms.

text.p: Russia's Federal Property Fund said on Friday there were no restrictions on foreigners taking part in a tender for 38 percent of Russia's Norilsk Nickel, but Uneximbank, which controls the stake, disagreed.
In a statement faxed to Reuters, the Fund said that according to information published by the Competition Commission in its "Reforma" bulletin, no restrictions were mentioned.
"According to the information published by the Competition Commission, no limits on foreign investors taking part (in the tender) have been introduced," it said.
The commission is in charge of the tender.
But officials at commercial bank Uneximbank, in control of the 38 percent, said a special decree was needed to allow foreigners to take part in the tender.
They said that as far as they were aware, no such decree had been signed.
Uneximbank has already said it intends to take part in the July 22 tender, which it is holding according to the terms of the shares-for-loans scheme under which it won the stake.
Russian equity analysts said the bank was likely to maintain control of the giant mining group, which this year is vying to become the world's biggest producer of nickel.
But analysts said major Western nickel companies could well be among foreign firms interested in buying into Norilsk if foreign companies were allowed to bid.

"If (the tender is open to foreign firms), this would open the way for...international rivals such as Inco Ltd and Falconbridge Ltd to participate, which could seriously influence the plant's position on the world market," Pioneer Securities said.
The Norilsk group is also a major producer of cobalt, platinum, palladium and copper.
"Firms like Falconbridge and Inco would certainly take a look (were they allowed to bid), but they would be very wary about what they were taking on," said a London-based nickel analyst.
Uneximbank has led a major restructuring programme at the group, aimed mainly at reducing its huge debts to various state and regional authorities and to its workers.
Norilsk announced ambitious production expansion plans earlier this year, targeting output of 213,000 tonnes in 1997, up 20 percent from 1996 levels.
Uneximbank announced on Monday it would sell its 38 percent stake in Norilsk in an investment tender. The stake represents 51 percent of voting shares.
The starting price for the stake is around $117 million. The winner would also have to invest $300 million in Norilsk and cancel debts worth around $70 million.
